title: Volcanoes of the world (hard)
intro: 10 volcanoes of the world, one after another. Put your marker as near as you can; the nearer, the more points. Only the coasts are drawn and the full-points circle is small, so this is the hard version.

rounds.name: Bora-Bericha-Tullu Moye
rounds.fact: Bora-Bericha-Tullu Moye is a pumice cone; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1900. The data places it in Ethiopia.

rounds.name: Frosty Volcano
rounds.fact: Frosty Volcano is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 2,012 m in the source data. The data places it in United States of America.

rounds.name: Taal
rounds.fact: Taal is a stratovolcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 2020. The data places it in Philippines.

rounds.name: Kaileney
rounds.fact: Kaileney is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 1,578 m in the source data. The data places it in Russian Federation.

rounds.name: Sulu Range
rounds.fact: Sulu Range is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 556 m in the source data. The data places it in Papua New Guinea.

rounds.name: Pico Basilé
rounds.fact: Pico Basilé is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 3,011 m in the source data. The data places it in Equatorial Guinea.

rounds.name: Ukinrek maars
rounds.fact: Ukinrek maars is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 91 m in the source data. The data places it in United States of America.

rounds.name: Mount Süphan
rounds.fact: Mount Süphan is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 4,058 m in the source data. The data places it in Türkiye.

rounds.name: Mutnovsky
rounds.fact: Mutnovsky is a complex volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 2,288 m in the source data. The data places it in Russian Federation.

rounds.name: Curtis Island
rounds.fact: Curtis Island is a volcano listed in the source data. The data places it in New Zealand.
